verdicts.evidence: Re-ran the auditor's reproduction (copied to scratch, 0.34 s): synthetic pack, Mars, target 95 deg. Full plan finished at 1,816 evaluations, its search finds 1 event (bracket -1319099.2487 s TDB). Plan starved to 605 evaluations: status budget-exhausted, admissible [-3283200,-1123200] (2,160,000 s), 1 unprocessed span. searchRetardedAberratedDeflectedOfDateOverPlan with acceptPartialPlan:true and maxEvaluations 4,000,000: status 'budget-exhausted' (inherited), events 0, searchEvaluations 0, spanResults 0, notSearchedSec 2,160,000, exhaustiveOverAdmissible false, mayHoldUnfoundSupportedEvents true -- identical to accept-partial.json. Extension: plans starved to 50/90/99 % of the full budget (classified admissible 3,283,200 / 5,875,200 / 6,480,000 s = up to 75 d) also return 0 searchEvaluations, 0 spanResults, 0 events. Code confirms the mechanism: partitioned-search.mjs:281-284 sets `status = plan.execution.status` before any subsearch, and runOn (line 340) is `if (status !== 'finished') { notSearched.push([lo, hi]); return; }`, so every span is skipped. The refusal text at line 199 ('pass acceptPartialPlan: true to search the part it did classify') and experimental.mjs:141 promise the search; types/experimental.d.ts:297-303 and README.md:251 only promise `finished: false` (accurate). The tier-a test partitioned-search.nodetest.mjs:169-187 pins status inheritance and asserts nothing about spans being searched. Result is honest (no wrong answer), so major, not blocking, is the right tier.

verdicts.correctedClaim: The partition's cos(elongation) enclosure over a 60-s Moon cell is ~2,900x the true variation (4.045e-2 vs 1.398e-5) and the ratio is constant in cell width, so at the declared 60-s tolerance the undecidable residue is ~2,900 cells per crossing whatever the tolerance (shrinking cells shrinks the residue only linearly, at the cell-count cost that PARTITION-RESULTS' 5-s sweep already shows breaks P-1). Decomposed by measurement: replacing the split R.pos-O.pos geocentric enclosure (domain-partition.mjs:315-329, widths 5,852/5,997/2,588 km) by the merged single-series form ((1+k)*moon, 124.5/126.3/42.4 km, true 18.3/58.3/18.9 km) cuts the cos width 44.8x to 9.0e-4; the remaining ~64x is the naive composition of -(e.d)/|d| in elongationCosInterval (deflection.mjs:178-180) -- even the exact sampled hull of d composes to 17x the true variation. PARTITION-RESULTS.md:105-123 misattributes the 0.042 width to how fast the elongation moves (the elongation's 12 deg/day gives only 1.4e-5 over 60 s). The same looseness governs the planets: Saturn F7's two coalesced boundary spans are 2,489 s and 2,658 s and Mars F5's 11,264 s and 12,192 s (40-200 floor cells per crossing). The retarded and aberrated rungs are NOT failing on the Moon (RETARDED-RESULTS 296,106 evaluations, ABERRATED-RESULTS A2 264,398, both finished), so the defect's practical impact is the deflected rung/partition (P-3, P-4, DEFLECTION-RESULTS Moon exhaustion at 4,000,001), not 'every retarded rung'. The projected ~0.04 d post-fix residue is an order-of-magnitude estimate: the same linear model predicts 40 d for the shipped enclosure against 15.8 d measured.
verdicts.evidence: Re-ran enclosure-width.mjs and moon-relative-state.mjs from scratch copies: floor crossing at TDB -701224266.695 s = 1977-10-12T11:28:05.3Z, 9.03 h before conjunction; at the crossing cell width 4.045e-2 vs true 1.398e-5 (2,892.7x), ratios 1,703.7x-8,859.4x over 24 cells, all 24 'boundary' though 20 are truly decidable (margins to 6.67e-3); split/merged/true widths reproduce to the printed digit at 60/600/3600 s. Own decomposition (decompose.mjs): split 4.045e-2 (2,892.7x), merged geometric 8.99e-4 (64.3x), merged + light-time mean-value term 9.03e-4 (64.6x), true hull of d 2.39e-4 (17.1x); all four enclose the sampled truth. Swiss as instrument (pyswisseph 2.10.03, flag 5746 with FLG_SWIEPH, ephe <swisslab>/ephe): light-time-only (NOABERR|NOGDEFL) Sun-Moon elongation at the alpha's crossing instant 4.9999997 deg vs the alpha's retarded elongation 5.0000000 deg (geometric 5.00547 in both); closest approach 0.3800 deg at 1977-10-12 20:27 UTC, matching PARTITION-RESULTS/DEFLECTION-RESULTS 0.381 deg 20:30Z; geometry and convention confirmed. Planet check (saturn-boundary.mjs -> planet-boundary.json): Saturn plan finished 10,268 evaluations, boundary spans 2,489.06 s and 2,657.81 s (0.0199 %); Mars 43,150 evaluations, spans 11,264.06 s and 12,192.19 s (0.0905 %); diagnostics.widestBoundarySec 42.1875 in both is the widest floor CELL, not a span. What the auditor got wrong: 'shrinking cells cannot fix it' contradicts PARTITION-RESULTS' own 5-s sweep (0.71 %) -- the residue scales linearly with cell width; the impact sentence about every retarded rung over-subdividing 'by roughly the same factor' was not measured and the retarded/aberrated Moon runs finished; the 0.04 d figure is a model, not a measurement. Severity major is earned: the Moon apparent-of-date deflected search is a documented FAIL that Swiss answers.

verdicts.correctedClaim: The alpha's proven (validated/experimental) modes support one operation, longitude crossings; the empirical mode adds a conditional 'aspect' kind (search.mjs SEARCH_CONTRACT.kinds). SEARCH_CONTRACT.notSupported (search.mjs:82-86) excludes stations, latitude/declination/distance/elongation events and rise/set/transit, and no eclipse or occultation operation exists anywhere in examples/precision-alpha/src. pyswisseph 2.10.03 offers solcross, mooncross, mooncross_node, helio_cross, rise_trans(_true_hor), sol_eclipse_when_glob/loc/how/where, lun_eclipse_when/_loc/how, lun_occult_when_glob/loc/where, heliacal_*, nod_aps and no station, aspect or geocentric planetary crossing finder -- so the alpha is below Swiss on eclipses, occultations, rise/set/transit and Moon node crossings (the material gap), and stations/aspects are an opportunity to exceed Swiss rather than a gap below it. Stations are roots of x*y' - y*x' (degree 2n-2 per piece); an aspect at angle theta is a root of a degree-2n bilinear polynomial whose roots include theta+180 deg and need a quadrant test; latitude crossings are roots of z_ecl. The claim that the partition 'already brackets elongation = 5 deg to 60 s' is false: coalesced boundary spans are 2,489-2,658 s for Saturn, 11,264-12,192 s for Mars and 10 spans totalling 15.8 d for the Moon (42.19 s is the widest floor cell). The production engine computes stations (src/lib/engine/transit-scan-core.ts stationBreakpoints) and eclipses (scripts/build-eclipses.mjs via astronomy-engine SearchGlobalSolarEclipse/SearchLunarEclipse) without completeness semantics, so the absence is in the proven layer, not the whole stack.
verdicts.evidence: search.mjs:77-86 read: kinds {longitude, aspect}, notSupported lists stations, 'latitude, declination, distance and elongation events', rise/set/transit; grep 'aspect' in validated-search.mjs: no hits, so no proven aspect kind. Swiss inventory run on the local pyswisseph 2.10.03 (swiss-check.py): finders exactly as listed above; no name matching station or aspect. Boundary-span widths measured by running planDeflectedDomain on the real pack for Saturn F7 and Mars F5 (planet-boundary.json) and taken from the Moon F2 reproduction (10 coalesced spans, 5.266 % = 15.8 d): elongation = 5 deg is not bracketed to 60 s by the current partition. Polynomial checks by hand: x*y' - y*x' has cancelling leading terms (degree 2n-2, as claimed); x1*y2 - y1*x2 and x1*x2 + y1*y2 are degree 2n, not 2n-2, and the bilinear form vanishes at both theta and theta+180 deg. Production capability by grep of the worktree (transit-scan-core.ts:231-265; build-eclipses.mjs:26-67). Severity stays major on the rule's 'capability gap below Swiss' clause because eclipses, occultations, rise/set and node crossings exist in Swiss and not in the alpha; the station/aspect portion does not by itself put the stack below Swiss.
